cases.note: The loop iterates thresholds from largest to smallest and breaks at the first satisfied threshold, exactly matching the original if/else chain, including the 'B' fallback. Behaviour is identical.

The mutant changed [-+]? to [^-+]? in the explicit int pattern, breaking !!int on signed binary literals like '-0b11' while admitting arbitrary junk lead characters; both branches of the test pass on pristine and fail on the mutant.

cases.note: The refactor is equivalent: slicing the prefix for 0b/0o/0x gives the same parseInt arguments as before, and the decimal path still passes the sign-prefixed string (or unsigned digits) to parseInt base 10, matching original behaviour.
The diff replaces `typeof val === 'string'` with `true`, so any non-string with a length property (arrays, String objects, etc.) is passed to parse() instead of throwing an error.
